title: CSV to XML – Name Your Root and Row Elements | OpenAnyDoc
description: Convert CSV to XML in your browser: one element per row, headers turned into valid tags, and <, > and & escaped. Copy it or download a .xml file.
heading: CSV to XML Converter
subtitle: Drop a CSV and its XML appears at once, one element per row, ready to copy or download as .xml.
intro: Turn a CSV export into XML for a system that only imports XML, a feed or a config file. Choose, drop or paste a CSV or TSV file and the XML is written at once: a root element holding one row element per line, with a child element per column named after its header. You can rename the root and row elements. Header names with spaces or symbols are turned into valid element names, and <, > and & in your data are escaped. The delimiter and encoding, Arabic Windows-1256 included, are detected for you, and the file is read in your browser, never uploaded.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your CSV is turned into XML by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees your data.

features.title: Valid XML every time
features.text: Header names become legal element names and special characters are escaped, so the file parses in any XML reader.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: Once this page has loaded, it keeps working without an internet connection.

stepsTitle: How it works: convert CSV to XML

steps.title: Add your CSV
steps.text: Choose or drop a .csv or .tsv file, paste CSV text into the box, or try a sample.

steps.title: Name the elements
steps.text: Keep <rows> and <row> or type the names your importer expects; the XML updates as you type.

steps.title: Copy or download
steps.text: Copy the XML to your clipboard or download it as a .xml file with the CSV's name.

handlesTitle: What the CSV to XML converter handles
handles: Files: .csv and .tsv, or CSV text you paste; comma, semicolon, tab and pipe delimiters detected.
Encodings: UTF-8, UTF-16 (when the file starts with a byte order mark), Windows-1256 Arabic and Windows-1252 Western European text, written out as UTF-8 XML.
Shape: <rows><row><column>value</column></row></rows>, with root and row names you choose.
Headers such as "Order ID" or "2024 total" turned into valid element names.
Escaping: <, > and & in cells written as <, > and &.
Quoted fields with commas or line breaks inside, as Excel and Google Sheets export them.
limits: Every value is written as text; the XML has no types, attributes or schema.
The preview shows the first 5,000 lines; Copy and Download always take the whole file.
faqTitle: CSV to XML: questions and answers

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The CSV is read and written as XML by your browser, on your device. Pasted text stays in this tab and is never sent anywhere.

faq.question: What does the XML look like?
faq.answer: A root element (rows by default) with one row element per CSV line; inside each row, one element per column named after its header, holding the cell's value.

faq.question: What happens to headers with spaces or symbols?
faq.answer: XML element names cannot contain spaces or start with a digit, so such headers are turned into valid names. The values under them are unchanged.

faq.question: Can I choose the element names?
faq.answer: Yes. Type a root name and a row name, for example products and product, and the XML is rewritten at once.

faq.question: Are numbers written as numbers?
faq.answer: XML has no number type of its own, so every value is written as text. A schema or the importing program decides how to read it.

faq.question: Does it work with large files?
faq.answer: Yes, though very large files can take a few seconds. The preview shows the first 5,000 lines; Copy and Download always take the whole XML.

faq.question: How do I convert a CSV file to XML?
faq.answer: Open or paste the CSV, type the root and row element names your importer expects, then copy the XML or download it as a .xml file. OpenAnyDoc writes the XML in your browser, so the file is never uploaded.
